from_quote: The House of Representatives is periodically elective, as in all the States; and for the period of two years
rationale: States the plan's term for the House of Representatives, "for the period of two years," the term set in this clause.

from_quote: The Senate is elective, for the period of six years
rationale: States the plan's term for the Senate, "for the period of six years," echoing this clause's "for six Years."

from_quote: The President is to continue in office for the period of four years
rationale: States the plan's term for the President, "for the period of four years," echoing this clause's "Term of four Years."
to_quote: during the Term of four Years

from_quote: The President of the United States is impeachable at any time during his continuance in office
rationale: Says the President "is impeachable at any time during his continuance in office," naming the impeachment provision for the President in this clause.

from_quote: The tenure by which the judges are to hold their places, is, as it unquestionably ought to be, that of good behavior
rationale: Names the judges' tenure under the plan as "that of good behavior," echoing this clause's "during good Behaviour."

from_quote: its absolute prohibition of titles of nobility, both under the federal and the State governments
rationale: Names the plan's "prohibition of titles of nobility" under the federal government, the prohibition in this clause.
to_quote: No Title of Nobility shall be granted by the United States

from_quote: its absolute prohibition of titles of nobility, both under the federal and the State governments
rationale: Names the plan's "prohibition of titles of nobility" under the State governments, the prohibition on the States in this clause.

from_quote: its express guaranty of the republican form to each of the latter
rationale: Names the plan's "express guaranty of the republican form" to each State, echoing this clause's words "guarantee" and "Republican Form of Government."
to_quote: guarantee to every State in this Union a Republican Form of Government

from_quote: the Constitution is to be founded on the assent and ratification of the people of America, given by deputies elected for the special purpose
rationale: Describes the Constitution's ratification by "deputies elected for the special purpose," echoing the word "ratification" of this article. Low because the paragraph describes the mode of ratification without naming the seventh article.

from_quote: The immediate election of the President is to be made by the States in their political characters. The votes allotted to them are in a compound ratio
rationale: Names the immediate election of the President by the States and the votes "allotted to them," the allotment of electors to each State in this clause.

from_quote: The eventual election, again, is to be made by that branch of the legislature which consists of the national representatives; but in this particular act they are to be thrown into the form of individual delegations
rationale: Names the "eventual election" of the President by the House of Representatives voting as "individual delegations," the procedure set out in this clause.

from_quote: If we try the Constitution by its last relation to the authority by which amendments are to be made
rationale: Takes up "the authority by which amendments are to be made" and "the mode provided by the plan of the convention," the amendment procedure of the fifth article.
